title: Concise skill-track cheat-sheets and inline task-driven onboarding
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Create a set of compact, skimmable 'skill-track cheat-sheets' that appear as contextual inline cards in the Console (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost views). These are short, task-oriented micro-guides designed to help an engineer or PM complete a single first-success activity (e.g., set up a rollout, add a cost alert, pin a model) without leaving the page.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-success for new and returning users by surfacing one actionable path per console surface.
- Keep UI density low: each cheat-sheet should be readable in < 30s and include at most 3 steps + 1 CTA.
- Support templated variations (beginner, power-user) and A/B experiments.
- Track activation metrics (click-through, completion, retention) so PM/Analytics can correlate with downstream usage (Dedicated sign-ups, deployment rollouts).

Scope of work in this ticket:
- Finalize content strategy for cheat-sheets across three surfaces: Dashboards (create first dashboard, pin route), Rollouts (canary setup quick path), Cost views (set up budget alert + preview cost card).
- Prototype compact cards (desktop + narrow tablet). Cards include title, 1-line rationale, 2–3 step checklist with microcopy, optional short gif, primary CTA, and 'try again later' snooze.
- Design two density modes: 'Minimal' (single CTA + progress) and 'Guided' (2–3 inline steps).
- Design accessibility states (keyboard focus, screen reader labels, contrast).
- Hand off tokens & CSS guidance to frontend (spacing, animation budget).
- Prepare test plan and success metrics to run with Growth for 4-week experiment.

Non-goals:
- Full onboarding flow or multi-step modals (those are separate PRDs).
- Heavy interactive tutorials or video walkthroughs (only 3–8s gifs allowed).

Trade-offs considered:
- Inline cards vs. modal deep-onscreen tours: inline is lower-friction and less distracting, but might be missed. We propose a timed, low-noise nudge pattern (first visit => show card; subsequent visits => toast + collapsed card).
- Visual complexity vs. discoverability: to avoid clutter we keep cards compact and provide a 'More tips' overflow that links to a full seed-playbook in the Help Center.

Design deliverables (this ticket):
- High-fidelity Figma prototype (desktop + narrow tablet) with two variants per surface.
- Copy deck with succinct step copy and microcopy alternatives for A/B.
- Component spec for frontend: token names, animation durations, aria attributes.
- Test plan stub for Growth including metrics and experiment variants.
tasks: Draft copy for 3 surfaces: Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost views
Create high-fidelity Figma prototypes (Minimal and Guided variants)
Review prototypes with PM + Growth and collect feedback
Produce component spec and handoff notes for frontend (spacing, tokens, aria)
Write A/B test plan and measurement definition for analytics
Prepare a small usability checklist and run 5 quick moderated sessions

Component spec included (tokens, animations, aria) and acknowledged by ENG-2021
Test plan defined with primary metric (activation completion rate) and secondary metrics (time-to-first-success, drop-off)
UX review sign-off from PM (Ana Patel) and Design Director (Priya Nair)
5 usability sessions completed and notes attached
